task:
I ran a differential expression experiment in one tissue and now want to know which curated gene sets are over-represented among the differentially expressed genes.

Files:
- data/de_genes.txt: the differentially expressed genes (one gene symbol per line, no header).
- data/detected_genes.txt: the genes detected in this experiment (one symbol per line).
- data/all_annotated_genes.txt: all annotated genes in the genome annotation used (one symbol per line).
- data/pathways.gmt: the gene sets, in GMT format (set id, description, then member symbols; tab-separated). Some members are symbols that are not in the current annotation.

Test each gene set for over-representation in the DE list with a one-sided hypergeometric test (equivalently, a one-sided Fisher's exact test), and control the false discovery rate with Benjamini-Hochberg across all gene sets tested. Only test gene sets that have between 10 and 500 members after restricting the set to the genes in your background; do not test the rest and do not count them in the multiple-testing correction. Report every gene set with BH-adjusted p < 0.05.

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{"enriched_gene_sets": []}
</EVAL_ANSWER>

where the list holds the ids of the significant gene sets (first column of the GMT).
design_source: Over-representation analysis with a whole-genome background instead of the genes detectable in the assay gives spurious enrichment of tissue-expressed gene sets (Timmons et al. 2015 Genome Biol; Wijesooriya et al. 2022 PLoS Comput Biol).
